review_candidates.description: About Perimeter The limit on superintelligence (SI) is no longer chips. It's power. New data centers wait years for a grid connection, while the office towers, hotels and hospitals of every major city sit on power they were built for and no longer use. Perimeter Compute is on a mission to put that power to work. We turn basements and mechanical rooms into GPU clusters, and our software links them into one inference network running inside the cities where SI will be used. Building owners earn from space that would otherwise sit idle. Frontier labs and inference providers get capacity without the years-long wait, a few miles from their users instead of a few states away. Perimeter is a small, highly leveraged team that has worked every layer of this problem: building GPU infrastructure at Lambda and HPE, engineering commercial buildings at Tishman Speyer and Trane, and routing inference at Subquadratic. The power is already there. Come build what runs on it. How We Work People make the decisions that matter. Agents do everything else. Agents write and review all of our code. People own the calls that are hard to undo: architecture, product direction, taste, and the frameworks we use to make those calls. Most decisions are two-way doors, so you make the call instead of waiting for one. If you like writing code yourself, you'll hate it here. One owner per outcome. You build it, you run it, you grow it. Roles here are bigger than usual. You'll do work that's normally split across engineering, product, sales and design. You'll work directly with customers to figure out what to build. You own the outcome, so you decide how to get there. If you want a clear ticket and someone else owning the result, this isn't the job. We Keep Reinventing How Software Gets Built. Code is a means to an end, not the end. We question every assumption. "Why?" is the most important question you can ask, and a rule nobody can answer it for gets deleted. How we build is code too. Every week, agents find what slowed us down and ship the fix. If you want a process that stays the same, look elsewhere. We build for agents as much as for people. Agents use our tools, APIs, docs and interfaces too. It isn't done until an agent can use it and recover from its errors without help. Every public API is defined once in code, and everything people and agents read about it is generated from that, so nothing drifts. Agents don't remember rules, so anything that matters is a check that fails, not a line in a doc. Because agents do the work, we can be prescriptive: one way to build things, and every agent follows it. If docs and error messages feel like someone else's job, we're not a fit. About The Role You'll own security for a cloud where customers will share our hardware and agents write all of our code. Attacks now move at machine speed: stolen keys can become a full compromise within hours, so our defense has to move faster. You'll run agents that attack our own infrastructure around the clock, starting in our digital twin (a software replica of a whole site where we can break things safely), and build detection and response that can contain a rehearsed attack in minutes. You'll start with what we run today, from our laptops and the agents on them to the pipeline they ship through, and grow into customer isolation as we build it. The job is to make the secure way the fast way: security that slows the team down has failed. You're measured on time to contain, time to a verified fix, how little you slow anyone down, and whether our red-team agents can get from one customer to another. What You'll Do Run a continuous agent red team against our digital twin, from the BMCs up through our APIs. Find what breaks first and get it fixed before it ships.
